working_title: Distinguishing preference mismatch from product failure
research_question: Can an LLM distinguish explicit preference mismatch from product defects and delivery complaints?
stake: A merchant needs different actions for unsuitable targeting, a defective product and delivery problems.
hidden_assumption: Review text contains enough explicit evidence for humans to distinguish these explanations.
competing_hypotheses: H1: Explicit context and aspect spans improve preference-mismatch classification.
H2: Sentiment and complaint keywords explain apparent gains without context reasoning.
H3: Humans cannot reliably separate these causes from available text.
discriminating_test: Compare majority/keyword baselines, text-only LLM and context/aspect-guided LLM under an equal model budget. Use two independent annotators plus adjudication; allow unclear and multiple labels. Split by parent product and remove exact duplicates; exclude listing aggregate ratings and reviewer identifiers. Report macro-F1, per-class recall, span F1, uncertainty coverage, product-cluster bootstrap intervals, cost and latency.
falsifier: No reliable human agreement, or no held-out improvement over the strongest baseline after controlling for sentiment and review length. Treat inconclusive intervals as inconclusive.
two_week_pilot: Days 1–3: refine schema on 50 reviews. Days 4–7: independently label 300 additional reviews across rating and completeness strata, including mixed-rating products and controls. Days 8–10: freeze schema and product-disjoint split; lock prompts on development data. Days 11–14: evaluate baselines and context ablation on untouched test products. Use pilot variance to plan a powered follow-up.
minimum_resources: Two annotators, one adjudicator, local review text, annotation budget; model access and cost approval before running LLM experiments.
strongest_reviewer_objection: This may be ordinary complaint classification; no independently verified customer fit or demonstrated novelty.
next_action: Review the 200-row annotation seed, extend it beyond rating-balanced sampling, and label the first 50 with uncertainty.
status: Provisional design; no experiment has been run.

research_question: Does evaluation only on complete listings overstate LLM interpretation performance?
stake: A shopping assistant evaluated only on complete listings may leave most of a merchant catalog untested.
hidden_assumption: Human labels can be sampled across completeness strata.
competing_hypotheses: H1: Restricting to complete listings changes measured LLM performance.
H2: Differences reflect review length, product type or review volume rather than completeness.
H3: Performance is stable across completeness strata.
discriminating_test: Sample independently labeled reviews in complete and incomplete product strata. Keep test products disjoint from development. Compare the same frozen model; report within-stratum macro-F1 and catalog-weighted estimates. Match or stratify on observable review length and volume; validate product types manually. Report residual confounding and do not interpret a stratum difference as a causal effect of missingness.
falsifier: No meaningful stratum difference, or the difference disappears under observable controls; either result limits the selection-bias claim.
two_week_pilot: Week 1: cross-tab eligibility and design a 300-review stratified annotation sample. Week 2: adjudicate, freeze prompts, evaluate a single fixed model and reweight to known catalog proportions. Report uncertainty and strata with insufficient labels.
minimum_resources: Same annotators and frozen model as Q1; extra labels may be necessary for sparse strata.
strongest_reviewer_objection: Observed groups are confounded, listing timestamps are unknown, and the pilot may be underpowered.
next_action: Audit the eligibility table and preregister the strata and estimand before looking at model scores.
status: Provisional design; no experiment has been run.
